nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge-Graph Workflow
nodes.rationale: Codebase questions are answered from a scoped subgraph (graphify query/path/explain) instead of raw grep or the full GRAPH_REPORT.md because the returned subgraph is much smaller and cheaper in context; `graphify update .` is AST-only so keeping the graph current costs no API tokens.

nodes.label: Laravel Boost (Agentic Development Tooling)
nodes.rationale: Laravel's predictable structure and conventions are claimed to make it well suited to AI coding agents; Boost exposes 15+ tools/skills so agents follow framework best practices.

nodes.label: robots.txt Open Crawl Policy
nodes.rationale: Default Laravel policy: `User-agent: *` with empty `Disallow:` allows every crawler on all paths; nothing is excluded.

nodes.label: PRD ERP + MES Manufaktur Pipa v3.0
nodes.rationale: v3.0 takes the existing application's database schema as its basis: table and field names are preserved verbatim and ALTERed only where ERP criteria demand, so migration from the legacy app does not require renaming.
nodes.norm_label: prd erp + mes manufaktur pipa v3.0

nodes.label: Single MySQL Database `ab-erp` for ERP and MES
nodes.rationale: The reference diagram's ERP-DB/MES-DB split is deliberately collapsed into one database so BOM, Master Item, WOS and WO are read directly with no cross-database sync, cache tables or outbox; the accepted trade-off is that an ERP/API outage takes MES down too, mitigated by HA MySQL plus the terminal offline queue.
nodes.norm_label: single mysql database `ab-erp` for erp and mes

nodes.label: Serial Number Traceability (RM 1:pcs, PM 1:lot)
nodes.rationale: Serials are generated up-front at GR creation (status GENERATED) so the GR document and QR labels can be printed before physical inspection; actual length/weight are captured later and all corrections (OK/NG/VOID) happen inside the GR, which keeps the master item free of locked weight/length values.

nodes.label: Dual UoM for Pipe RM (length mm + weight kg)
nodes.rationale: Each serial carries remaining_length and remaining_weight in parallel so consumption, costing and quota realisation can all be driven by actually measured values rather than master conversion factors.
nodes.norm_label: dual uom for pipe rm (length mm + weight kg)

nodes.label: Import Quota Control (ton per quota code)
nodes.rationale: Balance = total ton − open-PO reservation (estimate) − GRN realisation (actual). Import PO is hard-blocked when the balance is short (override only via a dedicated approval) because exceeding the customs quota is a regulatory breach, not a business preference; the estimate-vs-actual weighing difference auto-corrects the balance.
nodes.norm_label: import quota control (ton per quota code)

nodes.label: Scrap RM Candidate Rule (remaining < min BOM length)
nodes.rationale: Automatic flagging only proposes a candidate; the final decision stays manual and reversible in both directions (scrap ⇄ usable) with a recorded reason, because BOMs change and an offcut deemed unusable today may fit a future part.
nodes.norm_label: scrap rm candidate rule (remaining < min bom length)

nodes.label: Operator/Machine Rule (cutting 1 user multi-machine; non-cutting max 2/2)
nodes.norm_label: operator/machine rule (cutting 1 user multi-machine; non-cutting max 2/2)

nodes.label: FG Transfer via spec_group
nodes.rationale: Transfer between two FG codes is permitted only when spec_group matches, so physically identical stock can be re-badged for an urgent order without ever letting a different specification substitute silently; the move is approval-gated and carries value and lot traceability along.

nodes.label: FG Downgrade (NG finished good back to material)
nodes.rationale: Rejected FG re-enters stock as material via a mapped RM/PM code with freshly re-measured length/weight; the value gap is booked as a reclassification journal to scrap/variance so inventory value never silently inflates.
nodes.norm_label: fg downgrade (ng finished good back to material)

nodes.label: Multi-Level BOM (FG as PM of another FG)
nodes.norm_label: multi-level bom (fg as pm of another fg)

nodes.label: Period-Based FG Pricelist
nodes.rationale: A Sales Order pulls the price valid on its own document date; with no active pricelist the line is blocked and can only proceed via approval override, preventing ad-hoc pricing.

nodes.label: Multi-Vendor per Material (priority, MOQ, lead time)
nodes.norm_label: multi-vendor per material (priority, moq, lead time)

nodes.label: Subcontractor Portal & Virtual Location
nodes.rationale: Goods sent out for outside processing move to a virtual location 'Subcont-{vendor}' rather than leaving stock, because ownership and inventory value stay with the company; PPh 23 is withheld on the service invoice.

nodes.label: MES Offline Mode (PWA buffer + client_uuid idempotency)
nodes.rationale: Shop-floor scanning must not stop when the network drops, so payloads queue locally in IndexedDB keyed by client_uuid and replay on reconnect; server-side idempotency on that uuid is what makes replay safe against duplicates.
nodes.norm_label: mes offline mode (pwa buffer + client_uuid idempotency)

nodes.label: PPN under PMK 131/2024 (DPP Nilai Lain 11/12)
nodes.rationale: Non-luxury goods are taxed 12% on a 11/12 'other value' base (effective 11%); the rule is expressed as a per-tax-code formula with an effective date so a future rate change is configuration, not a code change.

nodes.label: Import Cost Sheet / Landed Cost per Actual Weight
nodes.rationale: Freight, insurance, duty, import VAT, PPh 22 and PIB/EMKL charges are allocated by actual weighed kg rather than by quantity, because pipe bars vary in weight and cost per kg is the only stable unit for later consumption costing.
nodes.norm_label: import cost sheet / landed cost per actual weight

nodes.label: Final Check Sheet (FCS / OQC traceability gate)
nodes.norm_label: final check sheet (fcs / oqc traceability gate)

nodes.label: Master WOS / Routing (cutting first, machine priority)
nodes.rationale: Pipe-part production always starts at Cutting, so routing sequence 1 is constrained to a cutting process whenever the BOM contains a per-pcs serialised RM; downstream steps consume WIP pallets rather than raw serials.
nodes.norm_label: master wos / routing (cutting first, machine priority)

nodes.label: General Store (non-material sparepart & consumable)
nodes.rationale: Sparepart issues are charged to a cost center and linked to a machine/asset so spare-part history per asset becomes an asset-control input; these items enter via a normal non-material GR without serials.

nodes.label: Existing Database Schema Baseline (m_/prc_/wh_/prd_/tr_ prefixes)
nodes.rationale: Legacy table and column names are kept verbatim (m_item, tr_cut_main, wh_out_main, …) so the running application's data can be reused without a rename migration; new modules (sales, accounting, costing, asset) are added in the same naming style.

nodes.label: FTPI Visual Identity & UI/UX Direction
nodes.rationale: Design tokens are extracted from the PT. Fusoh Tube Parts Indonesia site (clean Japanese corporate character, corporate blue and white) so the ERP shell reads as the customer's own system.

nodes.label: Naming & Data-Type Convention
nodes.rationale: Status columns use VARCHAR(30) plus a PHP Enum constant instead of a MySQL ENUM so new statuses can be added without an ALTER; measurements use DECIMAL rather than int/double to avoid float drift on lengths and weights.

nodes.label: Standard Status Workflow & State Machine
nodes.rationale: Every document follows DRAFT→SUBMITTED→APPROVED→RELEASED→PARTIAL→COMPLETED→CLOSED with per-document state classes; an illegal transition returns HTTP 409 so concurrent or stale UI actions cannot corrupt document state.

nodes.label: API Response Envelope & Business Error Codes
nodes.rationale: 422 for validation/business rules, 409 for state conflict and optimistic lock, 403 for permission, 423 specifically for accounting period lock — distinct codes let the frontend render the right i18n message from a single ErrorCodes registry.
nodes.norm_label: api response envelope & business error codes

nodes.label: Modular Monolith Structure (app/Modules + Core)
nodes.rationale: Modules communicate only through Service interfaces or Events — a controller may never touch another module's Model directly — so the monolith keeps module boundaries enforceable without paying the cost of separate services.

nodes.label: NumberingService (race-safe document numbers)
nodes.rationale: Numbers are allocated inside a transaction with lockForUpdate on the doc_numberings row and reset monthly by (doc_type, period), guaranteeing gapless unique doc_no under concurrency.

nodes.label: ApprovalEngine
nodes.rationale: Approval levels are generated from approval_flows keyed by doc_type and value range, so escalation thresholds are configuration; rejection marks the document REJECTED and SKIPs remaining levels rather than deleting rows, preserving the audit trail.

nodes.label: TaxEngine (calcVat)
nodes.rationale: Rates are resolved by effective date on the tax code; rounding is half-up to whole rupiah at document level (not per line) with the residual pushed to the last line, so the printed invoice total always reconciles.

nodes.label: JournalEngine (post)
nodes.rationale: Posting reads acc_journal_setup for Dr/Cr mapping per ref type, refuses a locked period with 423, asserts ΣD=ΣK, and is made idempotent by a unique key on (ref_type, ref_id, journal_type) so a retried job cannot double-post.

nodes.label: UomConversionService
nodes.rationale: For pipe RM the kg-per-mm factor is derived per serial from its own remaining weight and length, not from the master std_length/std_weight; master factors are used only for PO and MRP estimation, because real bars deviate from nominal.

nodes.label: SerialService (generateForGrLine, actualize, consume)
nodes.rationale: consume() deducts length and a proportionally computed kg from the serial and updates under an optimistic lock (WHERE id=? AND version=?), so two concurrent shop-floor scans on the same bar cannot both succeed on stale data.

nodes.label: QuotaService (reserve / actualize)
nodes.rationale: Balance is recomputed as total + SUM(ton*sign) under SELECT … FOR UPDATE on the m_quota row, serialising all reserve/actualize access; movements are stored as signed ledger rows rather than a mutable balance so the quota card is fully auditable.

nodes.label: ScrapService (evaluate / decide)
nodes.rationale: The minimum usable length is the MIN(length_per_pcs_mm) across all APPROVED BOMs using that component, cached for an hour and invalidated on BOM change, because recomputing it on every serial consumption would be a hot query on the shop floor.

nodes.label: MesDispatchService.resolve (TR_CUT vs TR_PRO)
nodes.rationale: Dispatch is decided by (sequence == 1 AND process.is_cutting): only the first cutting step scans RM serials; every other step — including a later cutting step — scans WIP pallet codes, because after step 1 the physical unit of handling is a pallet, not a bar.

nodes.label: TrCutService.record
nodes.rationale: Exactly one operator is enforced structurally by putting user_id on the main row (not a child table), while machines are a detail table since cutting is legitimately multi-machine.

nodes.label: TrProService.record
nodes.rationale: Each output pallet stores from_pallet_label and the source pallet flips to MOVED, giving a complete pallet-to-pallet chain across processes without needing per-piece serials after cutting.

nodes.label: WoAllocationService.book (serial booking to WO)
nodes.rationale: Booking pre-computes qty_per_serial = floor(remaining_length / length_per_pcs) plus projected remnant and scrap-candidate flags, so the operator only scans a prepared list; a booked serial is locked out of other WOs until released.

nodes.label: Putaway & Visual Warehouse Layout
nodes.rationale: Rack assignment after GR confirm feeds a drag-drop visual layout so remnant stock is always locatable — the stated fix for the legacy wh_rem behaviour where leftovers had no clear rack.

nodes.label: Fixes vs Reference Application Schema
nodes.rationale: Five deliberate corrections to the legacy design: integer FK to wh_serial.id instead of string serial numbers scattered everywhere; dual UoM (length AND kg, reference tracked length only); explicit status workflow instead of a boolean `finish` flag; DECIMAL for measurements instead of int/double; plus scan idempotency and standard audit columns.

nodes.label: Item–Customer Mapping Validation (m_item_customer)
nodes.rationale: Replaces the legacy single m_item.cus_id column with a mapping table: an SO line is rejected (422 ITEM_CUSTOMER_NOT_ALLOWED) unless the item is registered for that customer, and the same row supplies customer_part_no and qty_per_box for DO and packing labels.

nodes.label: GRN Serial Flow (generate → print → actualize → confirm)
nodes.rationale: AP invoice entry is deliberately gated until after GR confirm so the 3-way match runs against actual received qty, weight and length rather than PO estimates.
nodes.norm_label: grn serial flow (generate → print → actualize → confirm)

nodes.label: MRP Engine (low-level-code explosion)
nodes.rationale: Items are levelled by low-level code so an FG acting as PM is only netted after its parent; v1 simplifies pipe RM on-hand to kg plus std_length-equivalent bars rather than exact offcut packing, and import RM net kg is converted to ton and compared with quota balance to warn about quota shortage.

nodes.label: CRP Loading Calculation
nodes.rationale: Load is allocated to priority-1 machines first and cascades to the next priority on overload; residual overload is only flagged (suggesting OT, subcont or shifting MPS) rather than auto-resolved, keeping the planner in the loop.

nodes.label: COGM Calculation & Roll-Up per WO
nodes.rationale: COGM = material + labor + FOH + subcont − recovery, with material taken from actual serial movement kg × landed unit cost; an FG-as-PM lot is carried into the parent WO as material, which is what makes multi-level roll-up work.

nodes.label: FCS → RFG Receiving Flow
nodes.rationale: FCS creation validates that every operation is COMPLETED and all NG dispositioned before an FG lot may be received, and freezes a traceability JSON of serials used and operations performed.

nodes.label: Offline Terminal Design (service worker + IndexedDB queue)
nodes.rationale: Critical validations run locally against a WO/BOM/WOS snapshot downloaded at menu loading; the queue flushes in order per WO and a duplicate client_uuid returns 200 with meta.duplicate=true instead of erroring, so replay is safe. Offline is capped at 24 hours before a re-sync is forced, bounding how stale local validation data can be.
nodes.norm_label: offline terminal design (service worker + indexeddb queue)

nodes.label: Optimistic Locking & Explicit Row Locks
nodes.rationale: High-contention resources (quota, numbering, serial, wh_stock_sum) get explicit pessimistic locks inside DB::transaction, while user-facing document edits use a version column sent from the frontend — pessimistic where writes are short and hot, optimistic where a human holds the record open.

nodes.label: Security Design (Sanctum, 2FA, vendor guard, period lock)
nodes.rationale: Privileges are re-checked in the service layer as well as route middleware (defense in depth); the vendor portal uses a separate guard with a global vendor_id scope and shares no endpoint with internal users; MES terminal tokens are long-lived but bound to terminal_id plus an IP allowlist.
nodes.norm_label: security design (sanctum, 2fa, vendor guard, period lock)

nodes.label: Audit Trail & Structured Logging
nodes.rationale: A global Observer writes before/after JSON to audit_logs and the log is append-only with no update or delete endpoint, making it immutable by construction; X-Request-Id correlates frontend, API and queue jobs.

nodes.label: Queue Jobs & Scheduler (default | heavy)
nodes.rationale: MRP/CRP/COGM runs go to a separate `heavy` queue so long batch computations cannot starve interactive exports and alert jobs on `default`.

nodes.label: React Frontend Design (DataTable, DocForm, ScanBox)
nodes.rationale: One server-side DataTable and one header–detail DocForm are reused by every module so sorting, filtering, dirty-check and optimistic-lock behaviour stay uniform; the sidebar and action buttons are driven by the permission set returned from /auth/me rather than hardcoded per page.

nodes.label: API Contract (/api/v1 and /api/mes/v1)
nodes.rationale: RESTful resources plus action endpoints /{id}/{verb}; full contract is generated to OpenAPI 3 from annotations, and the frontend query hooks are auto-generated from that spec to keep client and server in step.

nodes.label: Subcont Flow (PO Subcont → DN → Receipt → AP)
nodes.norm_label: subcont flow (po subcont → dn → receipt → ap)

nodes.label: Deployment & Infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Migrations must be backward-compatible so blue-green deploys stay zero-downtime; a read replica absorbs report/EIS queries to keep the transactional primary responsive for shop-floor scanning.

nodes.label: Testing Strategy (Pest unit → Playwright E2E)
nodes.rationale: Unit tests target exactly the engines whose arithmetic is regulation- or money-sensitive (TaxEngine rounding, QuotaService balance, ScrapService threshold, SerialService kg proportion); UAT is driven from the 16 PRD user stories.

nodes.label: wh_serial / wh_serial_movement / wh_stock_sum Schema
nodes.rationale: wh_serial_movement is a per-serial ledger keyed by (ref_type, ref_id) giving full traceability, while wh_stock_sum is a denormalised aggregate maintained by events purely so list screens and MRP do not have to scan the movement ledger.
